notes.musome: Lisez: to the whole class. To one student: Lis.
notes.muwandiike: Écrivez: to the whole class. To one student: Écris.
notes.okubala: Les maths, short for les mathématiques.
notes.otegeera: Tu comprends ? Just raise your voice at the end.
notes.ddamu: Répète to a friend, Répétez to the teacher.

guidebook.intro: Follow lessons in class: instructions to the whole class, questions and homework. Teachers address the class with vous.

tips.title: Lisez, écrivez, écoutez
body: When a teacher speaks to the whole class, the verb ends in **-ez**: **Lisez le livre. Écrivez vos noms. Écoutez.** To one student: **Lis, écris, écoute.**
A student asks the teacher with **vous** too: **Répétez, s’il vous plaît.**

tips.title: Three ways to ask a question
body: In speech, just raise your voice: **Tu comprends ?** Or start with **est-ce que**: **Est-ce que tu comprends ?** In writing and polite speech, swap the verb and the subject: **Comprends-tu ?**
Two set phrases for language learners: **Comment dit-on … en français ?** (how do you say … in French?) and **Qu’est-ce que ça veut dire ?** (what does that mean?).

tips.title: J’aime les maths
body: School subjects take **le, la, les**: **les maths, les sciences, l’histoire, le français**. After **aimer**, keep them: **J’aime beaucoup les maths.** After **étudier**, too: **J’étudie l’anglais.**

culture.title: School in French
body: Across francophone Africa, many children study in French from primary school. The exams have names that every family knows, like **le BEPC** after middle school and **le bac** at the end of secondary school.
